reviewedFrom: EP14-01 (docs/enterprise-production/completion-checklist.json), docs/production-org-playbook.md (who advances each step), docs/books-revenue-recognition.md (home closing) and the HOME-01 expectations for the books half.

land-takedown.derivation: Ten lots of the first tranche cost $72,000 each, $720,000, paid from the operating account. Books records the purchase first: with Books as the ledger the takedown refuses to close on its expected price. Closing the takedown makes its ten lots owned and the land manager develops them, so ten lots are developed and the ten in later phases stay controlled; the two lots given a second, unpurchased tranche stay controlled. All $720,000 sits in land inventory (1120) and none has been spent on a house.

expected.closeWithoutLandPurchase: refused: record the land acquisition first

reservation-and-deposit.derivation: Lot 1 is held for the buyer by the sales consultant and reserved with a $20,000 earnest deposit, which creates the buyer's home (a production-posture project) and invoices the deposit. The buyer's check is received against that invoice, so $20,000 sits in customer deposits (2300) on that home. The lot is assigned. A land manager does not hold lots (sales.manage), and a second buyer cannot take a lot with a live reservation.

agreement-priced-and-signed.derivation: The Mangrove sells for $385,000 in this community; lot 1 carries a $15,000 premium; the buyer takes the extended garage ($18,500, structural) and three design choices ($4,800 + $7,200 + $2,600 = $14,600). Total $385,000 + $15,000 + $18,500 + $14,600 = $433,100. The agreement is saved as a draft, then executes: the contract is active at the quoted total, the reservation converts, the lead is won and a projected closing exists for the home. A second buyer's agreement on a stale quote hash is refused.

selections-by-cutoff.derivation: The buyer confirms kitchen, flooring and lighting at the catalog prices of the day: $4,800 + $7,200 + $2,600 = $14,600 price against $2,900 + $4,300 + $1,500 = $8,700 cost. The design coordinator moves the group's cutoff to yesterday; the group is locked, and a late change to a locked group is refused (it needs a change order).

start-gates-and-roles.derivation: A package opened for lot 1 has the plan-pinned gate passed (the agreement pinned it), the selections gate passed (the buyer's design group is already locked) and financing not applicable (cash buyer); the release produces the budget and PO set, so those two wait. The starts coordinator attests the permit, the plot plan is on file, the price book resolves in a dry run, and the coordinator gives final approval: the package is ready. A superintendent and a sales consultant cannot release (start.release).

release-creates-the-house.derivation: The plan's trades at the price-book rates: sitework $34,000, foundation $58,000, framing 1,650 sf at $44 = $72,600, plumbing $41,000, electrical $46,000 = $251,600. The three confirmed design choices are bought at cost from their trades: $2,900 + $4,300 to framing, $1,500 to electrical. By trade: sitework $34,000; foundation $58,000; framing $72,600 + $7,200 = $79,800; plumbing $41,000; electrical $46,000 + $1,500 = $47,500. Total $260,300; the budget is the same $260,300. Five trades, five orders, no open exceptions, and running the release worker again issues nothing more. The lot is started, the eight-step schedule is on the house, and the $72,000 of land has moved from land inventory to the house (1160).

built-and-billed.derivation: Each of the five orders is approved and its trade bills it in full, $260,300 in all. The bills are approved, so accounts payable (2000) holds $260,300, unpaid. The house holds the $72,000 land plus the $260,300 of cost in inventory under construction (1160): $332,300.

completion-and-closing.derivation: Completion moves the house's $332,300 (land $72,000 + construction $260,300) to completed homes (1170) and provides a $6,500 warranty reserve. The closing is settled at the contract price of $433,100; the buyer's $20,000 deposit is applied, leaving $413,100 due by wire. The sale relieves 1170 exactly by the cost it came from, one line per component: land and development $72,000 and construction $260,300, cost of sales $332,300; inventory and land are left at zero. Revenue is $433,100, gross margin $433,100 - $332,300 = $100,800. No deposit is left held. The four home controls tie to the ledger.

warranty-enrolled.derivation: Closing queues the home's warranty enrollment: one coverage record from the closing, effective on the closing date, carrying the program's three terms. The $6,500 reserve provided at completion is on the books (2260) and its control ties.

design-choices-open-after-signing.reason: Defect: signing a purchase agreement locks every selection row on the home, including the pending design rows it has just created, so the buyer cannot make a design choice after signing (executePurchaseAgreementFromEnvelopeExecution, lib/services/community-sales.ts, the project_selections update that sets locked_at). The lifecycle unlocks them by SQL to continue. Policy: design choices stay open until their group's cutoff; only structural options lock at signing.
design-choices-open-after-signing.derivation: After signing, none of the home's three design selections is locked.

purchasing-manager-reaches-a-house.reason: Defect: the purchasing manager role holds po.generate, commitment.approve and the rest of the purchasing keys but not project.read, and a project-scoped check passes only for a project member or someone with project.read (hasAllProjectAccess, lib/services/authorization-policy.ts), so the role is denied on every house (deny_no_project_membership). It is the only production role without project.read. Separately, row-level security on project_selections shows a home's selections only to project members and admins, so the design studio coordinator, who has project.read, still cannot list or confirm a home's selection group (confirmSelectionGroup reports it not found); the same cause is behind preview-matches-release.
purchasing-manager-reaches-a-house.derivation: The purchasing manager previews the house's purchase orders.

preview-matches-release.reason: Defect: purchase-order generation reads project_selections through the caller's own client, which row-level security limits to project members, so a preview run by anyone but a member or admin leaves out every selected-option line while the release (service client) includes them. The price_book gate passes on the preview and the release then fails on the option exceptions (lib/services/po-generation.ts runGeneration selections read).
preview-matches-release.derivation: The preview's total equals the total the release issues ($260,300).

agreed-options-reach-purchase-orders.reason: Defect: options chosen in the agreement quote are stored only in the contract snapshot; nothing creates a selection for the structural option, so its cost never reaches the budget or a purchase order (lib/services/community-sales.ts createPurchaseAgreement writes option_items to the snapshot only; po-generation sources are plan takeoff lines and confirmed project_selections).
agreed-options-reach-purchase-orders.derivation: The release buys the extended garage as well: $260,300 + $11,000 cost = $271,300.

presold-home-adopts-inventory-without-re.reason: Defect: reserving a lot creates the buyer's home with a placeholder fixed-price contract beside the purchase agreement. Books reads two primary contracts that earn revenue differently (percentage of completion and at closing) and refuses to adopt the home for inventory, or to post to it, until a controller proposes and a second member approves a revenue policy for each (lib/services/books/revenue-basis.ts, the 'earn revenue differently' refusal; lib/services/projects.ts prepareProjectBillingContract). HOME-01 builds its homes with the purchase agreement alone, which is why it never meets this.
presold-home-adopts-inventory-without-re.derivation: Adoption succeeds on the first attempt.

deposit-invoice-reaches-the-buyer.reason: Defect: convertHoldToReservation issues the earnest deposit invoice without recipients (the buyer's email is not passed as sent_to_emails), so delivery defers to the outbox with 'Add at least one recipient' and the buyer is never told. The reviewed-conversion path (prepareReservationConversionBundle) does pass them (lib/services/community-sales.ts convertHoldToReservation createInvoice call).
deposit-invoice-reaches-the-buyer.derivation: The deposit invoice carries one recipient, the buyer.

closing-completes-without-repair.reason: Defect: settling a home sold on a real agreement records the money and then fails to complete: the settlement keeps the whole agreement quote, while readClosedSettlementEvidence (lib/financials/closing-settlement-evidence.ts) keeps only the fields its schema names, so the digest recoverClosingCompletion compares (lib/services/closings.ts) never matches. Warranty enrollment and the handoff are never queued. HOME-01 hand-builds a quote with only the schema's fields, which is why it passes.
closing-completes-without-repair.derivation: The closing completes on the first settle.

agreement-signs-through-an-envelope.reason: The signing packet is a PDF in file storage and the invitation is an email; the stack has storage only under --storage-env. Execution runs through the same service the envelope-completion handler calls.

release-copies-the-plan-set.reason: The release's drawings step copies the plan version's plan-set PDF onto the house, which needs file storage. Without it that one step is settled directly and every other step of the release runs for real.
